claude_proposed_widenings.name: force_drop_object
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Con save failure requires the creature to drop the held/worn metal object. No v4 taxonomy atom covers 'release a held item': force_move is positional, apply_condition has no 'drop item' analogue, and this is a distinct mechanical concept (item-economy disruption) absent from the v4 effect atom list.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or drop the object if it can

claude_proposed_widenings.name: OngoingTrigger.on_caster_bonus_action
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Heat Metal lets the caster optionally spend a Bonus Action on each later turn to deal the damage again. No existing OngoingTrigger variant models 'caster opts to spend a Bonus Action.' The trigger is not passive (requires player choice + resource), not on_caster_turn_start (which fires unconditionally), and none of the other variants apply.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: you can take a Bonus Action on each of your later turns to deal this damage again if the object is within range

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Attachment target: creatures_in_contact_with_object
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell attaches to a metal object but deals damage to creatures in physical contact with it — not to the object itself. No existing Attachment variant or TargetSelection expresses 'all creatures currently in physical contact with the attached object.' The object attachment exists, but there is no way to redirect effects onto touching creatures.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Any creature in physical contact with the object takes 2d8 Fire damage when you cast the spell

claude_proposed_widenings.name: RiderExpiry.start_of_caster_next_turn
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The disadvantage rider expires 'until the start of your next turn' — the caster's turn start. The two existing RiderExpiry variants (target_uses_or_turn_start and end_of_next_turn) do not express 'start of the caster's next turn.' This is semantically distinct: Sap's expiry tracks the target's use or the attacker's turn start; Heat Metal's expiry tracks the caster's turn start unconditionally.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the start of your next turn
